data.title: BNB Chain Describes Payment Lane for Transfers on BSC
data.description:
BNB Chain announced on X that Payment Lane reserves capacity for qualifying BNB transfers between wallets when BSC is busy. The reserved space is intended to keep unrelated activity, including trading and activity from other apps, from using all available capacity. Token payments may also qualify after they are approved for the lane.

The post distinguishes between having capacity available and knowing when that capacity is used. It says available space can help, while apps with deadlines also need precise information about when the reserved space is consumed. The announcement does not specify approval criteria for token payments or provide further technical details about how the lane works.

data.title: CAS20 and Jenner Add Token Controls as BNB Chain Develops New L1
data.description:
BNB Chain announced on X that CAS20 will give token creators standard tools to manage transfer permissions, set how many tokens exist and pause transfers. The post says Jenner adds the underlying capability for these functions. Together, the changes are described as part of continued work on BSC as BNB Chain develops its new L1.

CAS20 is presented as the set of tools for creators to control who can transfer tokens, determine the number of tokens that exist and pause transfers. Jenner, in turn, is identified as the capability underlying those controls. The announcement links the CAS20 tools and Jenner’s supporting functionality, describing them together as ongoing development work on BSC in the context of BNB Chain’s new L1. It does not specify a release date or provide further technical details about the upgrade.

data.title: Patrick McHenry Accepts Partial Responsibility for Stalled U.S. Crypto Market Structure Legislation
data.description: Former U.S. House Financial Services Committee Chairman Patrick McHenry said he shares some responsibility for the failure to advance market structure legislation, adding that the crypto industry missed its best opportunity to pass it. According to Odaily, McHenry discussed why the Clarity Act stalled, shortcomings among crypto industry participants and lawmakers, and how the industry should prepare for Democrats to take control of Congress in January.

data.title: Machi Big Brother Sells Bored Ape 32 for 12.5 ETH, About $28,000
data.description: Machi Big Brother sold Bored Ape 32 on OpenSea for 12.5 ETH, worth about $28,000. According to Odaily, Onchain Lens tracked the sale.

data.title: Polymarket's AJ Dybantsa Points O/U 9.5 Yes Probability Rises 30 Points
data.description: On Polymarket, the Yes probability for the “AJ Dybantsa: Points O/U 9.5” submarket in the “Wizards vs. Hawks” event rose from 57% to 87%, a 30-percentage-point increase. According to ChainCatcher, the change occurred over the past hour.

data.title: Polymarket’s Spurs vs. Kings Sabonis Rebounds Yes Odds Rise 18.5%
data.description: On Polymarket, the “Yes” option in “Spurs vs. Kings” for “Domantas Sabonis: Rebounds O/U 7.5” rose from 50% one hour ago to 68.5%, an increase of 18.5 percentage points. According to ChainCatcher, the odds shifted sharply.

data.title: The Corner Store to Bring SoHo Concept to the Las Vegas Strip
data.description: Catch Hospitality Group is opening a Las Vegas location of The Corner Store at the Cosmopolitan, according to Bloomberg. Co-founder and partner Eugene Remm said the 150-seat restaurant will preserve the intimacy and authentic SoHo experience of its 75-seat New York original, rather than offer a Vegas-specific or watered-down version.

data.title: Mexico Approves Six Solar Projects to Add Nearly 650 MW of Capacity
data.description: Mexico's Energy Ministry approved six solar power projects with private partners, expected to add nearly 650 megawatts of capacity to the country's strained grid. According to Sina Finance, the projects are estimated to require more than $750 million in investment and are expected to generate 1,881 gigawatt-hours annually, with battery storage facilities; private partners submitted them in the second round of Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission renewable energy project auction.

data.title: STOCKS | Sweetgreen CEO Neman Says Sales Momentum Improved After Cyclospora Traffic Hit
data.description: Sweetgreen CEO and co-founder Jonathan Neman said sales momentum improved after a summer Cyclospora outbreak that was unrelated to the company’s stores but reduced traffic across the sector, according to Bloomberg. Sweetgreen reported about 5% comparable-sales growth in October after comps returned to flat in September, with further improvement in early November.

data.title: STOCKS | Elanco Rises Nearly 8% After Q3 Earnings Beat, Outlook Increase
data.description: Elanco Animal Health shares rose nearly 8% after third-quarter earnings topped expectations and the company raised its full-year outlook, according to Bloomberg. CEO Jeff Simmons called it a high-quality quarter, citing 11% reported growth and broad strength across markets and product lines during an interview on “The Close.”

data.title: 6 US Stocks to Watch After Wall Street's $2.5 Trillion Crash
data.description: Nasdaq market value fell roughly $2.5 trillion Thursday as investors sold AI stocks; a modest Friday rebound failed to prevent a fourth straight weekly decline. According to BeInCrypto, NVIDIA, Vistra, Amazon, Alphabet, Uber and Netflix are stocks to watch based on earnings, valuations and Wall Street forecasts. NVIDIA fell 9.3% Thursday despite revenue doubling to $96.2 billion; Vistra gained 10.5% Friday as adjusted EBITDA rose 50%. Amazon cloud revenue grew 39.3%, Alphabet revenue rose 25% and cloud sales more than doubled, Uber bookings climbed 20% with $2.5 billion in free cash flow, and Netflix revenue grew 12%. All six have bullish consensus ratings, though infrastructure restrictions, heavy spending, weaker guidance and slower ad growth pose risks.

data.title: FIGS CEO Trina Spear Says Demand Outstrips Supply as Results Beat Estimates
data.description:
FIGS reported third-quarter revenue of $190.7 million, above the $182.8 million estimate, and top- and bottom-line results exceeded expectations, according to Bloomberg. The company recorded a fourth consecutive quarter of at least 25% revenue growth. Non-scrubwear revenue rose 35%, and international revenue also increased.

CEO and co-founder Trina Spear said health care professionals are buying more FIGS products beyond scrubs, including underscrubs, compression socks and outerwear, for work and off-duty wear.

data.title: AI | Groq Executive Targets Doubling Valuation to $8 Billion Amid AI Selloff
data.description: A Groq executive has launched a bid to double the data center operator’s valuation to $8 billion in about three months, according to Bloomberg. The executive criticized rivals for relying too heavily on debt markets.

data.title: Hyperliquid Burns $1.64 Million Worth of HYPE in 24 Hours, Repurchasing 21,040 Tokens
data.description: Hyperliquid repurchased and burned 21,040 HYPE in 24 hours, worth $1.64 million, at an average price of $77.93. According to Odaily, Onchain Lens reported the figures.

data.title: Arini Flagship Fund’s Year-to-Date Loss Widens to 32% as It Sells Holdings
data.description:
Arini Capital Management’s flagship hedge fund’s year-to-date loss widened to 32% by the final days of October, and it sold some holdings.

According to Sina Finance, citing a letter to investors, the fund, which focuses on high-yield debt, lost 19.7% in October amid continued weakness in credit markets. Managed by Hamza Lemssouguer, the fund reassessed its five largest positions, which together represented about two-thirds of its net asset value.

The fund received $389 million in inflows over the past week, part of its $1.5 billion fundraising. The letter said the fund had underestimated dislocations in the CCC-rated bond market, which accounted for most of its exposure and led to strong co-movement among portfolio positions. The fund cut some positions and reduced total leverage to its lowest level since early 2022, while planning to further diversify its portfolio.

data.title: AI | AI-Animated Feature 'Gods Don’t Give Gifts' Set for Theaters
data.description: The AI-generated animated feature Gods Don’t Give Gifts is heading to theaters. Fable Studio CEO Edward Saatchi said a team of 30 people spent nine months creating the film, which relies on human directors, writers, voice actors and artists, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Paraguay Senate Removes President Santiago Peña Over Banking Scandal
data.description: Paraguay's Senate voted unanimously to remove President Santiago Peña over a banking scandal on Friday, Senate TV reported. According to Sina Finance, citing Senate TV, the impeachment motion passed with 44 votes in favor and one abstention.

data.title: Tom Lee Sees 15% Nasdaq Rally as JPMorgan's Jack Caffrey Calls AI Rout Normal
data.description: Fundstrat’s Tom Lee said he would buy the AI-stock dip and expects a 15% Nasdaq rally, while JPMorgan Asset Management portfolio manager Jack Caffrey called the selloff normal. The Nasdaq-100 fell 6.36% and erased $2.3 trillion in value a day earlier, according to BeInCrypto. Caffrey said companies he met this week had 12- to 24-month order backlogs. On Friday, US payrolls rose 165,000 in October, versus roughly 65,000 expected, lifting bets on a December Fed rate hike.

data.title: Circle Mints 250 Million USDC on Solana
data.description: Circle minted 250 million USDC on Solana, and Solscan data shows the transaction was executed by Circle’s minting address. According to Odaily, Whale Alert recorded the mint at 6:06 (UTC+8).

data.title: Ukraine Clarifies Budanov Will Attend Ukraine-U.S.-Russia Talks but Will Not Lead Delegation
data.description: Ukraine President's Office Chief Budanov will attend trilateral talks with the United States and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, but will not lead Ukraine's delegation. According to Sina Finance, citing China Media Group, presidential press adviser Litvin said on November 6 that Budanov had only confirmed he would travel to Abu Dhabi with the Ukrainian delegation, not that he would lead it; Ukraine's negotiating team was preparing for the talks, and the parties had held several rounds of discussions on arrangements that day.
